headline: ASX closes up 0.6% on a solid Sunday, Pilbara Minerals surges 4% and GTA VI buzz lifts Take-Two — while Iran's six-month war milestone rattles global markets.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a strong session today, jumping 4.1% to $5.36. No specific news catalyst in the data, but lithium stocks have been sensitive to any hints of improved demand from China and EV battery makers. Still well below your buy-in, but today's bounce is a welcome sign of life. Long-term thesis around the lithium cycle remains intact.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft surged 1.68% in last night's session to $513.53, and it's been on a tear — up about 6.3% recently on the back of blowout Q4 results. Azure cloud revenue is being powered by AI demand, with the company reporting that AI-related workloads are growing faster than anyone expected. Sitting on a solid 15.9% gain overall in your portfolio.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google climbed 1.53% last night to $342.88, riding the same AI cloud wave as Microsoft. No specific news catalyst, but AI-fuelled tech optimism has been broad-based across the NASDAQ names. Up 11.5% overall for you — the long-term ad-and-cloud story is tracking well.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two rose 1.03% last night to $235.39, directly linked to excitement around the GTA VI 'extended look' preview that dropped this weekend. Rockstar also broke its silence on earlier leaks, calling them 'heartbreaking' but the game is clearly generating enormous hype. The stock is now barely in the green on your overall position — patience here is key.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up 0.18% today to $16.31, a quiet session. The ETF tracks AI-focused companies globally, so it broadly benefits from the Microsoft and Google AI momentum — but it's still down 13.6% from your purchase price. The AI sector story is long-term, and today's move is just noise.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up 0.25% today to $93.93. Emerging markets have been a mixed bag — the ongoing Iran conflict and Middle East tensions are a headwind for some EM economies, while China's recovery remains patchy. You're marginally in the red overall — nothing to worry about for a long-term ETF holder.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG added 0.23% today, a steady session. This fund holds a broad mix of global and Australian shares, so it moves with the overall market mood. A quiet but positive day — up 0.6% overall for you.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS edged up 0.16% today to $528.61, reflecting the ASX's positive mood as it prices in last night's mixed US session. The underlying US market was slightly down on the NASDAQ last night, but your ASX-listed version had a calm day. Up 2.5% overall — solid long-term hold.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals (PLS.AX) — big bounce today, but still deeply underwater
watch_today.detail: PLS surged 4.08% today to $5.36, which is a great single-day move. But you're still down 20.5% overall on this position. The lithium market recovery is gradual and uncertain. Nothing has fundamentally changed — hold what you have and only consider adding if you believe in the long-term lithium cycle story and want to average your cost down.

watch_today.title: Microsoft (MSFT) — AI cloud story is firing on all cylinders
watch_today.detail: MSFT is up 1.68% last night and ~6.3% in recent weeks after crushing its Q4 earnings. Azure cloud growth driven by AI workloads is the engine. You're sitting on a 15.9% gain. For a long-term holder there's no reason to touch this — it's doing exactly what you bought it for.

watch_today.title: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) — GTA VI hype is real, but be patient
watch_today.detail: The GTA VI 'extended look' dropped this weekend and the internet went wild. Rockstar called earlier leaks 'heartbreaking' but the game is generating enormous anticipation. TTWO rose 1.03% last night to $235.39. You're barely in the green overall (up 1.4%). The big payoff here is when GTA VI actually launches — this is a classic hold-until-the-catalyst play.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF still in the red despite sector tailwinds
watch_today.detail: GXAI is up just 0.18% today and still 13.6% below your purchase price. The AI sector is absolutely booming (see MSFT and GOOG), but this ETF hasn't fully caught up. For a long-term holder, the thesis is still intact — global AI adoption is accelerating. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: RBA still jittery on inflation — watch for rate signals this week
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank has flagged ongoing concern about inflation risks, according to the WSJ. This matters for your ASX holdings and the broader economy — if the RBA stays hawkish (keeps rates higher for longer), it puts pressure on Australian growth stocks. No immediate action needed, but keep an eye on any RBA commentary this week.

watch_today.title: Iran war at six months — oil and gold volatility worth watching
watch_today.detail: Six months into the Iran conflict, gold fell 1.73% last night and oil is largely flat at $83.40. Markets seem to be adjusting to the 'new normal' of Middle East tension rather than panic-buying safe havens. Your VGE emerging markets ETF has some exposure to countries affected by this — nothing to act on now, but worth monitoring.

world.summary: The six-month mark of the Iran war is dominating global headlines, with Iran's new supreme leader calling for Muslim unity against the US and Israel, while Turkey and Israel jostle for regional influence. Back in the US, Trump's targeting of political opponents and the upcoming midterms are ramping up political tension.

stories.title: Six months of war in Iran — what's changed and what's at risk
stories.why_it_matters: Reuters has mapped out six major consequences of six months of war in Iran — including surging oil price volatility, a refugee crisis spreading into neighbouring countries, and new geopolitical alliances forming across the Middle East. For everyday Aussies, the war is putting upward pressure on global energy prices and contributing to inflation fears worldwide. Iran's new supreme leader has specifically called for Muslim solidarity against the US and Israel, signalling the conflict is deepening rather than winding down.

stories.title: Iran's new supreme leader calls for Muslim unity against US and Israel
stories.why_it_matters: Iran's newly installed supreme leader has publicly called on Muslim nations to unite against the United States and Israel at the six-month anniversary of the war. This is a significant escalation in rhetoric that risks drawing more regional powers into the conflict. It also raises the stakes for global oil supplies — Iran sits on major oil and gas reserves, and any wider regional conflict could push energy prices sharply higher, affecting petrol prices and inflation in Australia.

stories.title: Turkey and Israel vie for Middle East influence as tensions spike
stories.why_it_matters: As the Iran war reshapes the Middle East, Turkey and Israel are both manoeuvring to fill the power vacuum and extend their regional influence. Turkey, as a NATO member and large Muslim-majority nation, is in a delicate position — trying to maintain ties with Western allies while appealing to Muslim solidarity. This geopolitical jostling raises the risk of the conflict spreading beyond Iran's borders, which would have significant consequences for global stability and energy markets.

stories.title: Middle East war fallout: World Bank fears job losses and rising poverty in Bangladesh
stories.why_it_matters: The World Bank has warned that the Middle East conflict is creating ripple effects far beyond the region, with Bangladesh facing the prospect of significant job losses and rising poverty. Bangladesh relies heavily on garment exports and remittances from workers in the Gulf states — both of which are being disrupted. It's a reminder that this war isn't just a regional issue; it's creating a humanitarian and economic shockwave across developing economies.

stories.title: Trump administration targets political opponents including James Comey
stories.why_it_matters: ABC News has published a list of individuals being targeted by the Trump administration, including former FBI Director James Comey. The list spans political figures, officials, and others seen as critics or obstacles to the current administration. This kind of institutional pressure on former officials is raising alarm bells about the health of US democratic checks and balances — a concern that's also playing into investor sentiment around US political stability heading into the midterm elections.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a solid session today, gaining 0.6% to close at 9,092. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 dipped 0.25% and the NASDAQ fell 0.52% — a slightly soft night despite strong individual performances from tech names. Gold dropped sharply by 1.73% as investors appear less panicked about the Middle East situation than in recent months. Oil was flat at $83.40. The Aussie dollar softened slightly to US71.6 cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid close — broad-based gains across the market.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Slight dip last night — markets treading cautiously.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech index slipped last night despite strong individual stocks like MSFT and GOOG.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Essentially flat — the Iran war isn't spiking oil prices as sharply as many feared.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold fell sharply last night — investors appear to be less fearful than recent weeks, pulling back from the safe-haven trade.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar dipped slightly — a softer AUD is a small tailwind for your USD-denominated holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) when converted back to AUD.

politics.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia is the main domestic story today, signalling it's still on guard about inflation — which has implications for interest rates and the cost of living for everyday Australians.

stories.title: Reserve Bank of Australia signals continued caution on inflation
stories.why_it_matters: The Wall Street Journal is reporting that the RBA remains 'jittery' about inflation risks, suggesting the central bank is not yet ready to confidently declare the inflation fight is won. This matters for everyday Australians because it means interest rates could stay higher for longer, keeping mortgage repayments elevated. For investors, a cautious RBA also signals that the economy isn't getting a near-term boost from rate cuts — which can weigh on consumer spending and growth stocks listed on the ASX.

ai.summary: The AI world this weekend is dominated by two big themes: a major cybersecurity warning from 100 companies including OpenAI and Anthropic about AI-powered attacks, and the growing debate about whether governments are regulating AI fast enough — from chatbots to medical devices to synthetic biology. Plus, a handy deal for everyday AI users.

stories.title: 100 companies including OpenAI and Anthropic warn of escalating AI cyberattacks
stories.why_it_matters: One hundred major tech companies — including AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic — have jointly warned that AI-powered cyberattacks are escalating at an alarming rate. The concern is that the same AI tools making your life easier are also being weaponised by hackers to write more convincing phishing emails, break through security systems faster, and launch attacks at massive scale. This is one of the biggest security challenges of the AI era, and it's putting pressure on governments to act quickly — and on cybersecurity companies, which are seeing a surge in demand.

stories.title: OpenAI and Nvidia CEOs to speak at tech-focused G20 meeting
stories.why_it_matters: The CEOs of OpenAI (Sam Altman) and Nvidia (Jensen Huang) are set to address a technology-focused G20 meeting, putting AI at the very centre of global economic policymaking. This signals that world leaders are treating AI as a top-tier economic priority, not just a tech curiosity. For investors in AI-adjacent stocks (like your GXAI.AX ETF, MSFT, and GOOG), this kind of high-level government engagement tends to legitimise the sector and can lead to more public investment and clearer regulatory frameworks.

stories.title: FDA seeks public input on regulating AI medical devices
stories.why_it_matters: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is now asking the public to weigh in on how to regulate AI tools used in medical devices — things like AI that reads X-rays, monitors patient vitals, or helps diagnose diseases. This is significant because AI in healthcare is moving faster than the regulations designed to keep patients safe. If the FDA gets this right, it could unlock enormous growth in AI-powered medicine; if it gets it wrong, patient safety risks could slow the whole sector down.

stories.title: Siemens CEO warns against over-regulating AI
stories.why_it_matters: The CEO of German industrial giant Siemens has pushed back against what he calls excessive AI regulation, arguing that too many rules too quickly will stifle innovation and put Europe and other markets at a competitive disadvantage against the US and China. It reflects a real tension playing out globally right now: regulators want guardrails, but businesses argue the rules are moving too fast. This debate will shape how quickly AI can be deployed in industrial and enterprise settings — which matters for stocks like MSFT and the broader GXAI ETF.

stories.title: One subscription to get GPT, Claude, Gemini and more — for $30/year
stories.why_it_matters: A new $30-per-year subscription deal is giving users access to multiple top-tier AI chatbots — including OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini, and Perplexity's Sonar — all in one hub. That's seriously cheap for what you get. If you're not already using AI tools in your daily life or work, this kind of bundled access makes it very easy to experiment. Competition between AI models is also driving quality up and prices down fast.

sport.summary: Round 26 of the NRL is done and dusted — the top eight is now locked in after a big weekend of footy. The Rabbitohs cemented their finals spot with an emotional win, the Sharks' top-four hopes are officially dead, and the Warriors ran riot over the Knights. In AFL, Carlton is rolling in the wildcard round.

stories.title: NRL top eight locked in — Tigers' horror moment seals the final spot
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL's top eight is now set after Round 26, with the Wests Tigers' finals campaign ending in heartbreak after a 'horror moment' — Cowboys beat them 24-10 at Queensland Country Bank Stadium. The Storm also impressed, thrashing the Broncos 46-20 at Suncorp on Thursday night. Finalists are confirmed; now it's all about seedings heading into the first week of September.

stories.title: Rabbitohs lock in finals berth with emotional Arrow tribute and Latrell's return
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney Rabbitohs beat the Gold Coast Titans 42-22 on Saturday to seal their finals spot in an emotional match that featured a tribute to the late Lote Tuqiri (Arrow). Latrell Mitchell returned from injury in timely fashion, providing the class and power the Rabbitohs needed. The Titans were hammered at Cbus Super Stadium — tough news for Gold Coast fans.

stories.title: Eels thrash Sharks 38-18, ending Cronulla's top-four dreams
stories.why_it_matters: The Parramatta Eels produced a stunning 38-18 demolition of the Cronulla Sharks at CommBank Stadium on Sunday, completely ending the Sharks' hopes of finishing in the top four. It was described as an 'electric' ambush, with the Eels looking like a genuine finals contender. The Sharks now face a must-win finals series just to stay alive in their campaign.

stories.title: Knights prop sent off for 'savage' hit that KO'd young Warriors player
stories.why_it_matters: A Newcastle Knights prop was sent off during the Warriors vs Knights match in Auckland on Sunday (Warriors won 46-32) after a 'savage' hit that knocked out a young Warriors player. It was one of the ugliest incidents of the season and will almost certainly result in a lengthy suspension from the match review committee. The Warriors' big win puts them in strong shape heading into the finals.

stories.title: Carlton keep rolling in AFL wildcard round
stories.why_it_matters: Carlton continued their strong form in the AFL wildcard round with another victory, driven by what's being described as their 'Batman and Robin combo' — likely Cripps and another key forward pairing. The Blues are building serious finals momentum, though AFL fans are raising concerns about the wildcard round format, especially after two notable retirements were announced this weekend. Carlton's winning run is one of the feel-good stories of the AFL season.
